summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and chronic respiratory conditions was admitted for green, blood-tinged sputum, dyspnea, and throat pain. She had no fever, stable vital signs, and normal white blood cell count. A chest X-ray showed no acute process, and ENT tracheoscopy revealed no signs of tracheal inflammation or infection. Given the absence of bacterial infection markers, antibiotics were withheld, and she was managed symptomatically for an acute upper respiratory infection. Her chronic pain was controlled with home medications, and she remained stable. She was discharged home with instructions to monitor for red flag symptoms and to follow up with ENT. Chronic issues, including iron deficiency anemia and diarrhea, were noted for outpatient follow-up.
